value: temperature was the main factor that affected shoot mortality in a warming and nutrient mesocosm (P < 0.05)
method: mesocosm with 12 glass aquaria (500 L), four treatments (control, temperature, nutrients, nutrients plus temperature); shoot number counted at the beginning and end and the net change expressed as a percentage; three-way ANOVA with post hoc tests
conditions: Plants from two sites (Bacoli, relatively eutrophic, EU; Ischia, relatively oligotrophic, OL), two fragments of 15 to 20 connected shoots per basket, one basket per site per tank, three aquaria per treatment (aquarium is the experimental unit, n = 3); control 24 C, warmed tanks raised 0.5 C per day to 30 C; five weeks; nutrients and temperature are crossed so the temperature contrast is made in both nutrient states; site-level two-way ANOVA (Table 1) gives a temperature effect on shoot mortality in EU plants (P = 0.01) but not in OL plants (P = 0.31); mortality values are net shoot change, the highest being -41.6% in EU plants under T and -15.7% in OL plants under T, shown graphically by treatment; relative growth rate showed no significant differences between plant groups or treatments (OL RGR fell about 30% under T, not significant); the paper itself describes timepoints T1 to T4 inconsistently between Methods and a supplementary caption; a single warm treatment level (30 C) was tested

source.authors: Pazzaglia J, Santillán-Sarmiento A, Helber SB, Ruocco M, Terlizzi A, Marín-Guirao L, Procaccini G
source.title: Does Warming Enhance the Effects of Eutrophication in the Seagrass Posidonia oceanica?

quote: Temperature was the main factor that affected shoot mortality along the experiment (P < 0.05).
note: Whole-plant shoot mortality against a 24 C control tank under a 30 C treatment; a physiological endpoint with no thermoreceptor identified, and the shoot-count change is a loss of shoots, not a signalling response. The sentence pools two sites; Table 1 shows the temperature effect on shoot mortality is significant only in the EU site.
